summary: Plan gate cold read after T1 shipped and after PR 503 corrected the plan and spec. Twelve findings: four genuine decisions put to Ravi (sequential graph, scope owners for the /new event and the resolved route, cleanup evidence and the hashed id, the column-naming deviation) and the rest resolved from the repository against what T1 actually shipped. Amended once; frontier closed.
gaps: T1's task block said all four callers switch to retireProviderSession and put the compaction-delta call site in its write scope, contradicting decision 0159 §4 and the new helper's `active`-row predicate.
T1's write scope could not produce its stated work: it omitted group-agent-runner.ts, the runtime-app files and package.json while naming the unchanged compaction-delta call site.

The partial-usage contract named a nonexistent DeepAgentTurnFailure wrapper, said usage is attached to an error, omitted both inline lanes, and carried a reviewer rule that the shipped Claude QueryFailure contradicts.

The plan claimed T1 carries the resolved DeepAgents registry route; the shipped code still sets modelRoute from input.provider, and D-0083 transferred the work without T2's scope covering the runner input contract.

Surface Impact called the API 'Unchanged by design' although limits.provider_session_max_input_tokens changes the typed JSON that /v1/settings/desired-state accepts and returns, and no round trip proved the field survives that surface.
Parked scope (per-request seam and capacity cap, delta snapshot, DeepAgents largest-not-summed billing) had no deferral rows and was postponed to a future story-close action.
The plan body digest had moved to ef00438d while the approved and decomposed digest remained 279a4a3c, and the plan still labelled itself approved.
contradictions: The approved parallel graph (T2 and T3 depending on T1 only) is not independently buildable: T3 needs the cleanup event type and runner drain that T2 owns, and merging T2 first activates the ceiling against a no-op drain, orphaning checkpoints until T3 lands.
The /new retirement event required by the spec had no owner: all event behaviour was assigned to T2, whose scope excludes both /new handlers, while T3 owns the handlers and claimed no event work.

Cleanup failures could leave no evidence at all — cleanup_failed is published best-effort with no fallback log or publication-failure test — and `sha256(id)` did not name which id, where hashing the internal provider-session id would break the documented operator join.
The physical column context_high_water_mark deviates from constitution/pnp-database-standards.md:46, which requires camelCase, with the deviation recorded nowhere.
resolutions: T1's block now names THREE switched callers (fingerprint, missing-session, ops-service facade and its canonical-ops-repo twin) and states that compaction-delta keeps expireProviderSession unchanged per 0159 §4, because it operates on a `ready` row the new helper's `active` predicate would not match.

T1's write scope corrected to the files that actually shipped — group-agent-runner.ts, the two runtime-app bootstrap files, provider-session-measurement.ts, canonical-ops-repo.postgres.ts and package.json — with the compaction-delta call site marked explicitly NOT in scope.

The partial-usage passage rewritten to the shipped contract: DeepAgentPartialUsage IS the thrown value with no wrapper type, a close-driven abort keeps its identity with the usage riding on it, denials and denial-driven aborts carry usage, both inline lanes emit one terminal error output, and the reviewer rule now describes both carriers accurately.

Ravi's decision: T2 takes the resolved registry route with the host-to-runner input contract added to its write scope (D-0083); the plan now states plainly that T1 sets provider and modelRoute from the same value and resolves cache policy at provider granularity.
API reclassified as Changed with the payload-shape change spelled out, and a PUT/GET control-API round trip over /v1/settings/desired-state added to the Verify Plan as T2's proof.

Recorded as D-0086 (per-request seam and capacity cap), D-0087 (delta snapshot) and D-0088 (largest-not-summed billing), each with its own trigger; Surface Impact now cites the ids instead of promising a story-close action.
The plan is being re-grilled and re-saved against the amended body for a fresh human approval, after which the decomposition rebinds to the new digest.

Ravi's decision: the graph reverts to SEQUENTIAL T1 -> T2 -> T3, the only order where each task is independently buildable and the ceiling never runs against a no-op cleanup drain. The plan already declared this order; the decomposition is what rebinds.
Ravi's decision: T3 publishes session.provider.retired for /new because it owns both handlers, while T2 keeps the event types and every other publication. Both task blocks now say so.

Ravi's decision: the hash is over the RAW EXTERNAL session id (never the internal provider-session id, which would silently match nothing in the documented join), and a structured error log carrying that hash plus the sanitised cause fires when cleanup_failed publication itself fails, with a test driving that path.

Ravi's decision: decision 0160 written and accepted, recording snake_case physical columns as this repository's deliberate deviation; the plan attests it in frontmatter and cites it at the column definition.

rounds.question: The grill says the T2 ∥ T3 parallel graph you approved is not independently buildable: T3 needs the cleanup event type and runner drain that T2 owns, so a T3 branch cut from T1 alone cannot typecheck or falsify its ceiling/fingerprint/missing-session proofs. And in the other direction, merging T2 first switches on the default ceiling while the cleanup drain is still a no-op, orphaning DeepAgents checkpoints until T3 lands. How should the graph run?
options: T3 depends on T2 — run sequentially (Recommended)
Keep parallel, add an integration order
Keep parallel, move the shared surface into T1's follow-up
rounds.chosen: T3 depends on T2 — run sequentially (Recommended)

rounds.question: Two runtime surfaces have no task owner. (a) The spec requires `session.provider.retired` after commit for `/new`, but the plan gives all event behaviour to T2, whose scope excludes both /new handlers, while T3 owns the handlers and claims no event work — so cleanup could ship without the required event. (b) D-0083 transfers the resolved DeepAgents route to T2, but T2's plan scope does not include the runner input contract it needs. Who takes them?
options: T3 takes the /new event, T2 takes the route (Recommended)
Defer the route, assign only the event
rounds.chosen: T3 takes the /new event, T2 takes the route (Recommended)

rounds.question: A constitution gap the grill flagged: the coordinator catches cleanup errors and publishes `session.provider.cleanup_failed` best-effort, but nothing specifies a structured fallback log or a publication-failure test. If both the cleanup and the event publication fail, an orphaned checkpoint leaves no evidence at all — which the no-swallowed-errors and structured-logging rules forbid. Separately, the plan says `sha256(id)` without naming which id; hashing the internal provider-session id instead of the raw external-session id would break the documented SQL join.
options: Require a structured fallback log and name the id (Recommended)
Fallback log only; leave the id to the implementer
rounds.chosen: Require a structured fallback log and name the id (Recommended)

rounds.question: The plan adds the physical column `context_high_water_mark`, but constitution/pnp-database-standards.md:46 requires camelCase physical columns. Every existing column in this repo is snake_case, so the repo convention looks like a deliberate long-standing deviation — but neither the plan nor any decision records it, so the grill counts it as an undocumented constitution violation.
options: Record the deviation in a decision (Recommended)
Note it in the plan only
rounds.chosen: Record the deviation in a decision (Recommended)

rounds.question: Closing round for the cache-bug plan grill. Your four decisions are applied: sequential T1->T2->T3; T3 publishes the /new retirement event while T2 takes the resolved-route plumbing; a structured fallback log plus a publication-failure test with the hash named as the RAW EXTERNAL session id; and decision 0160 written and accepted for snake_case columns. The other seven I resolved from the repo: T1's caller list cut to three with compaction-delta explicitly out of scope (0159 §4); T1's write scope corrected to the files that actually shipped, with the compaction call site marked NOT in scope; the partial-usage contract rewritten to what shipped (DeepAgentPartialUsage thrown directly, abort identity preserved, both inline lanes, QueryFailure for Claude); the resolved route marked as NOT delivered by T1; the API surface reclassified Changed with a PUT/GET round trip added to the Verify Plan; and the three parked items recorded as D-0086, D-0087 and D-0088 with triggers. Any remaining gap before I record the pass and save the plan for your approval?
options: No remaining gap, record and save (Recommended)
Show me the seven before recording
rounds.chosen: No remaining gap, record and save (Recommended)
